name: Bengali Ghugni
subtitle: white peas stewed soft with fried coconut slivers and a dust of roasted spice

ingredients.qty: 1 large finely chopped, plus 1/2 finely chopped raw for the top

ingredients.note: narkel kuchi, fried in the oil first
1 tsp for the tempering, 1/2 tsp dry-roasted for the finish
one for the tempering, one dry-roasted for the finish
or a squeeze of lemon at the table
in the soaking water, for peas that refuse to soften

prepNotes: Soak the white peas overnight in plenty of water with 1/4 tsp baking soda. Old peas can take a full 12 hours and will still be stubborn without it.

Pressure-cook the drained peas with the turmeric, salt and 500ml water for 3 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own. They should be soft enough to crush between two fingers but not shapeless.
Dry-roast 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli until they smell toasty and grind them coarse. This bhaja moshla is sprinkled over at the end and is not optional if you want the real thing.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds.
Fry the coconut slivers over medium heat for about 90 seconds, until they turn light brown at the edges, and lift them out.
steps.tip: They colour suddenly at the end. Take them out a shade paler than you want.

steps.text: Fry the diced potato in the same oil for 5 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Add the bay leaf, 1 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and fry for 8 minutes, stirring, until deep gold at the edges.
Stir in the ginger paste and cook 1 minute, then add the tomato with the chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 minutes until the oil separates.
steps.tip: Mash the tomato against the pan as it goes; you want no pieces left, only masala.

steps.text: Tip in the cooked peas with their liquid, the fried potato, the sugar and salt, and the remaining 100ml water.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, crushing a ladleful of peas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
steps.tip: Ghugni should be thick enough to sit on a spoon, not pour off it.

steps.text: Stir in the tamarind pulp and slit chillies and cook 2 minutes more, then check the salt.
Serve in bowls topped with the fried coconut, raw chopped onion, coriander, a dusting of bhaja moshla and garam masala, with lemon wedges alongside.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens as it sits. Reheat with 3 to 4 tbsp water and add the coconut, raw onion and bhaja moshla fresh each time.
